answer: The Cowan Paradox is a real thing. It’s been hiding in plain sight for decades. And it’s about to make your life as a founder, operator, or individual contributor a lot harder. The paradox is named after a psychologist named Robert Cowan. He published a paper in 1970 called “The Paradox of the Efficiency of Effort” that described what happens when you give people better tools. The basic idea is simple: when you give someone a tool that makes their work easier, they don’t do less work. They do more work. And they’re happier for it. That sounds counterintuitive, right? If I give you a magic eraser that makes your job 10x easier, wouldn’t you just… take a nap? Or at least work 20% less hard? No. What actually happens is this: You get more done. You take on more projects. You volunteer for more initiatives. You work longer hours. You’re more productive. You’re more valuable to your organization. And you’re happier. Because you can see the impact of your work. Because you can feel the sense of accomplishment. Because you’re not drowning in drudgery. The Cowan Paradox is why people who get a new car often work longer hours. Why people who get a new house often take on more responsibilities. Why people who get a promotion often work harder than they expected. It’s why the best teams always find a way to do more with the same resources. They’re not lazy. They’re just more effective. They’re more efficient
